title: C Foundations: Memory, Pointers & Strings
concept: Learn how programs really use memory with C23: types and overflow, arrays, pointers, strings and their terminators, malloc and free, structs and reading input safely.
description: A beginner course for people who can write a little code and want to know what their programs really do with memory. Every lesson starts from an incident in the C programs behind Lotus Mart's warehouse scanners and label printers - a stock report with 4294967295 boxes of tea, a weekly total that changes on every run, a return that never reaches the shelf count, a customer name that eats the city on a shipping label, a recent-scans list that shows one product three times, a log tool that gives up after 1,000 scans, a quantity prompt that loops forever, a fragile mug with a normal label - and fixes it with C23: integer types and overflow with ckd_add, arrays and half-open ranges, pointers and pointer arithmetic, strings, terminators and snprintf, malloc and free, structs and a growable array, fgets and strtol, and the new bool, nullptr, constexpr and typeof. Every bug is reproduced and found with gcc warnings, AddressSanitizer and UBSan. 8 lessons with quizzes and C coding challenges.
